stories.title: MMCM and CerCarbono issue first ELV carbon credits
stories.summary: Meta Materials Circular Markets and CerCarbono have issued the world's first carbon credits from End-of-Life Vehicle material recovery at COP31. The project covers 20 vehicle scrapping facilities across India, generating 24,988 credits. The companies describe the move as a significant milestone for circularity-linked carbon finance.

stories.title: Mercer Middle School integrates mass timber
stories.summary: The new 180,000-square-foot Mercer International Middle School in Seattle features mass timber construction and ground source heat exchange wells. Designed to house 1,000 students, the three-story building replaces an aging campus. The project consolidates fragmented facilities to provide space for native landscaping.

stories.title: Magicbricks releases sustainable real estate index
stories.summary: Magicbricks and the School of Planning and Architecture in Delhi have launched the Sustainable Real Estate Opportunity Index 2026. The report assesses ten Indian cities across six parameters, including environmental risk and infrastructure capacity, to determine their readiness for sustainable development and potential for risk-adjusted investment returns.

stories.title: China faces rising urban waste slurry volume
stories.summary: China produces over 300 million cubic meters of urban waste slurry annually, with volumes increasing by 10 percent each year due to rapid urbanization. Traditional disposal remains land-intensive, prompting concerns as the nation pursues carbon neutrality goals. The construction sector is currently managing the byproduct's environmental impact.

stories.title: MSCI GLOBAL GREEN BUILDING (^700753-USD-STRD) Seasonal returns chart - Yahoo Finance UK
India reports record solar open access growth
stories.summary: India added 8.4 gigawatts of solar open access capacity in the first nine months of 2026, a 29 percent increase over the same period last year. Growth was driven by captive ownership models and long-term power purchase agreements. Rajasthan led state-wise installations during the third quarter.

stories.title: Climate change increases risks for UK heritage sites
stories.summary: The Environment Agency estimates 6.3 million properties in England are at risk of flooding, a figure projected to reach eight million by 2050. Many historic buildings are located in flood-prone areas. Repairs are costly, as fixes must meet conservation standards and use appropriate materials.

stories.title: Amazon commits $7 billion to Indian renewable energy
stories.summary: Amazon plans to invest an additional 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030, bringing its total commitment to 11 billion dollars. The company also announced four new utility-scale wind and solar projects. It remains one of the country's leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy.

stories.title: Measuring the performance of commercial buildings - Construction Week India
Mass timber gains traction in construction
stories.summary: Mass timber, made of glued lumber layers, is increasingly used by architects as an alternative to steel and concrete. While material costs may be higher, developers cite potential savings during the construction phase. The material is currently emerging as a popular choice in the building market.

stories.title: IIT Delhi improves sustainability ranking
stories.summary: IIT Delhi rose to 194th globally in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027, up from 205th. The institute attributes its improved score to campus operations, including net-zero water use and waste elimination targets. The ranking provides a visible measure of progress for its institutional sustainability programme.

stories.title: Poche Aesthetics targets luxury home design
stories.summary: Poche Aesthetics is positioning itself in the Delhi luxury residential market by focusing on resolving designs on paper before construction begins. The firm aims to address the common disconnect between architects, interior designers, and contractors during the building process. It is currently considered a notable name in the region.

stories.title: High court halts Jaypee Greens construction
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered an immediate freeze on new construction and third-party rights across 236.87 acres of land at the Jaypee Greens Golf Course in Greater Noida. The interim order follows a petition filed by the Jaypee Greens Golf Members Association against the state government.

stories.title: Gurugram seals luxury buildings for commercial use
stories.summary: Gurugram authorities have sealed dozens of luxury residential buildings along Golf Course Road and in DLF Phase 1. The action follows court directives to enforce land-use rules and protect residential infrastructure. The enforcement wing of the Department of Town and Country Planning carried out the operation.

stories.title: Chennai revives Olympic city development plans
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu has restarted planning for an Olympic city at Semmancheri in Chennai, alongside five sports centres of excellence. The Public Works Department has invited architectural firms to prepare master plans and designs. The Olympic city project is slated for a 124.31-acre site.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu initiates Olympic infrastructure tender
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has invited architectural firms to design an Olympic city in Chennai and five centres of excellence across the state. The proposed city will occupy 124.31 acres at Semmancheri, while the centres will cover a combined 64.5 acres. The project has received a fresh lease of life.

stories.title: Puravankara launches Kochi residential project
stories.summary: Puravankara Limited has launched Purva Cityspire in Kochi with an estimated gross development value of 2,000 crore rupees. The company expects 40 percent of demand to come from non-resident Indians. Despite geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East, the developer reports no dip in housing demand in the region.

stories.title: Magicbricks index ranks city sustainability
stories.summary: Magicbricks and the School of Planning and Architecture in Delhi have launched the Sustainable Real Estate Opportunity Index 2026. The report ranks ten Indian cities based on their readiness for sustainable development and potential for risk-adjusted returns. It was unveiled at the India Habitat Centre in New Delhi.

stories.title: Indian museums seek global recognition
stories.summary: Two Indian museums have received international awards within weeks of each other, including the Red Dot: Best of the Best for the Anant Anadi Vadnagar Archaeological Experiential Museum. Officials hope the honors will transform museums from educational homework into weekend destinations for the average family.

stories.title: Godrej Properties faces closure order in Gurugram
stories.summary: The Haryana State Pollution Control Board has ordered the closure of a Godrej Properties housing project in Gurugram, citing lapses in dust-control measures. The developer also received a penalty from Tamil Nadu RERA regarding a separate advertisement. The company has not commented on the regulatory actions.

stories.title: Energy efficiency conference held in Visakhapatnam
stories.summary: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency and the Andhra Pradesh State Energy Conservation Mission hosted a two-day conference in Visakhapatnam to review building energy programs. Officials emphasized the need for better coordination among government departments and increased technical capacity to support the implementation of sustainable building standards.

stories.title: India Biennale 2026 to span 108 days
stories.summary: The Ministry of Culture will host the India Biennale 2026 from December 4 to March 21, utilizing 22 heritage sites, museums, and galleries across Delhi. The event aims to integrate art, architecture, and design into a single cultural initiative. The city is currently preparing for the arrival.

stories.title: Bank of England manages £160m headquarters revamp
stories.summary: The Bank of England is undertaking a £160 million renovation of its historic London headquarters. Governor Andrew Bailey faces the challenge of overseeing the complex project while maintaining the central bank's reputation for fiscal prudence and avoiding the budget overruns seen in similar international institutional upgrades.

stories.title: Buddhist memorial features suspended concrete cylinder
stories.summary: Architecture practice ASSISTANT has designed a memorial at the 12th-century Fukuden-ji temple in Japan. The structure, known as The Perpetual Care Grave, combines rammed-earth walls with a groundwater basin and a concrete cylinder suspended over the water. It is intended to provide a permanent site for reflection.

stories.title: Timber district planned for Thun, Switzerland
stories.summary: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for four timber buildings in Thun, Switzerland. The 13,000-square-meter development will feature stacked wooden volumes housing two hotels and residential units. The design aims to shape the entrance to the city's new Siegenthalergut district while overlooking the Bernese Alps.

stories.title: Modular gallery built in Indonesia
stories.summary: AT-LARS completed the Pertamina MotoGP Experience Gallery in Indonesia using a modular scaffolding system as its primary load-bearing framework. Designed and constructed in four months, the 1,400-square-meter pavilion prioritizes adaptability and reuse over the permanence typically associated with conventional museum architecture.

stories.title: Tree-top sauna wins architecture award
stories.summary: The Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna in Kanagawa, Japan, has been named architecture project of the year at the 2026 Dezeen Awards. Judges described the biophilic structure, which is built around living trees, as minimalist and spiritual. It also received the award for leisure and wellness project.

stories.title: Cotswolds barn converted into flexible space
stories.summary: ConForm Architects has renovated a former cattle barn in the Cotswolds into a multifunctional space for a working farm. The project, named Open Byre, contrasts the original red-brick and timber structure with modern zinc and black-timber additions to create a flexible space for meetings and guest accommodation.

stories.title: Minneapolis building slated for hotel conversion
stories.summary: The former Northwestern National Life Insurance Company headquarters in Minneapolis is set to become a 165-room hotel. Developed by CDT Realty Corp, the project involves ESG Architecture and Kelly Wearstler Studio. Construction is expected to begin in fall 2027, pending the necessary historic preservation approvals.

stories.title: New arena planned for Nitra, Slovakia
stories.summary: Architecture firm CHYBÍK + KRIŠTOF has been selected to design a multifunctional arena in Nitra, Slovakia. The proposal aims to integrate the facility into an open park located beneath the historic Nitra Castle. The arena is intended to host ice hockey and other indoor sporting events.

stories.title: Speculative tower house uses 3D-printed blocks
stories.summary: Barry Wark Studio has designed Tùr House, a speculative residential project intended for upstate New York. The structure would be composed of dry-stacked, 3D-printed sand blocks aligned with pins. The design features a library and living room at the top to provide views of the tree canopy.

stories.title: Workshop renovated into contemporary residence
stories.summary: Architect Akio Isshiki has converted a former sheet-metal workshop in Tatsuno, Japan, into a private residence. The renovation retains elements of the building's industrial past while reorganizing the interior space to fit within the constraints of the compact, historic castle town site.

stories.title: Villa N&N completed in Ivory Coast
stories.summary: Designed by SAOTA, the 860-square-meter Villa N&N is located on the edge of the Ébrié Lagoon. The residence features a design focused on balancing privacy with views of the Plateau business district skyline, utilizing a contrast of materials and an emphasis on spatial light relationships.

stories.title: Coal gangue used in pervious concrete
stories.summary: Civil engineers have demonstrated that replacing up to 30 percent of blast-furnace slag with coal gangue powder can create functional pervious concrete. The material is intended for use in urban sponge city infrastructure to manage stormwater, as conventional binders often face issues with flowability and structural capacity.

stories.title: Fabric formwork reduces concrete usage
stories.summary: MIT researchers have developed a software-driven method to cast concrete beams using fabric formwork. The technique reportedly reduces the amount of concrete required by two-thirds and steel reinforcement by half compared to conventional production. The resulting beams feature narrow, angled legs to maintain structural load-bearing capacity.

stories.title: Study reviews mass timber species
stories.summary: A systematic review of 189 peer-reviewed articles has evaluated the structural characteristics of mass timber products like cross-laminated timber. The research explores the potential for expanding the current range of wood species used in manufacturing to support the growth of low-carbon, high-strength construction projects.

stories.title: Atomik AM and CONCR3DE launch CoBound HiC binder for SiSiC 3D printing
stories.summary: Atomik AM and CONCR3DE have launched CoBound HiC, a binder for silicon carbide 3D printing. The product is characterized by high carbon content and is optimized for binder jetting, a process used for ceramics and other materials. Silicon carbide is known for its thermal stability and hardness.

stories.title: WASP brings upgraded ceramic and robotic 3D printing tech to Formnext 2026
stories.summary: WASP will introduce an upgraded ceramic Continuous Feeding System at Formnext 2026, featuring twice the material output of its predecessor. The manufacturer is also showcasing a 120 degree Celsius locally heated pellet printer and a robotic extruder. The technologies target ceramic serial production and technical polymer processing.

stories.title: Renda and Nexalus launch liquid-cooled AI server
stories.summary: Renda and Nexalus have launched the Nova8, a 4U AI server featuring eight liquid-cooled Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. The design allows the server to fit into standard 19-inch air-cooled racks without requiring additional cooling infrastructure. It is aimed at facilities not originally built for liquid cooling.

stories.title: ICON begins printing its largest commercial building
stories.summary: ICON has started 3D printing a 1,175-square-meter exhibition and training center for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio. The project uses the company's Vulcan construction system and pairs printed walls with a steel superstructure. Completion is scheduled for summer 2027, marking ICON's first full design-build commercial project.

stories.title: Sharjah Architecture Triennial explores civic infrastructure
stories.summary: The third Sharjah Architecture Triennial, curated by anthropologist Vyjayanthi Rao, runs from 14 November 2026 to 14 April 2027. Under the theme Architecture Otherwise, the event features works like bamboo and cloth bricks and aims to open discussions on how urban life and civic infrastructure could be imagined differently.

stories.title: Bamboo scrimber dowels outperform laminated bamboo in timber connections
stories.summary: Researchers found that bamboo scrimber dowels achieved a bending yield strength of 68.29 megapascals, outperforming thick strip bamboo panel dowels by 77 percent. The study evaluated bio-based connectors paired with Canadian spruce-pine-fir lumber to determine their potential as structural connectors within modern timber assemblies.

stories.title: VulcanForms orders 200 EOS M4 ONYX metal 3D printers
stories.summary: VulcanForms has placed an order for 200 EOS M4 ONYX 3D printers, the largest single order in EOS history. The announcement follows the company's disclosure of $500 million in financing to build three new factories. The new production sites will be fully integrated and use the metal printers.

stories.title: Researchers turn simulated moon dust into 3D printed bricks
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Arkansas have developed a method to 3D print interlocking building blocks from simulated moon dust. The process uses heat to fuse the material without the need for adhesives like glue or cement, exploring construction methods for future lunar settlements.

stories.title: Hyderabad agency removes 46 illegal borewells
stories.summary: The Hyderabad Disaster Response and Assets Protection Agency removed 46 illegal borewells and seized 31 water tankers near city lakes between June and October. The enforcement drive targeted four locations, with Sunnam Cheruvu accounting for the highest number of seizures and removals during the crackdown on groundwater extraction.

stories.title: Karnataka seeks review of E20 ethanol rollout
stories.summary: Karnataka has requested a review of the E20 petrol rollout, citing concerns over potential over-blending and the need for fuel outlet recalibration. In a letter to the Union petroleum minister, the state government stated that it supports ethanol blending but opposes any compromises on consumer welfare.

stories.title: HYDRAA plans groundwater recharge measures to prevent urban flooding
stories.summary: HYDRAA officials are identifying sites for new lakes and stepwells to improve groundwater levels and capture rainwater. The initiative aims to reduce flood risks in Hyderabad by increasing recharge capacity. Discussions focused on areas with varying groundwater levels and rainfall volumes to determine optimal capture locations.

stories.title: NHAI uses recycled materials for national highway network
stories.summary: The National Highways Authority of India reports using 1,559 lakh tonnes of recycled material since 2024. Fly ash and pond ash from thermal plants account for 1,532 lakh tonnes of the total. The remainder includes demolition rubble, steel slag, plastic, and bamboo used in road embankments.

stories.title: Maharashtra Maritime Board approves consultants for Mumbai water metro
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Maritime Board has approved project management and environmental consultants for the first phase of the Mumbai Water Metro. A joint venture of Tissa India and RINA Consulting was selected for project management, while Building Environment India was chosen for environmental consultancy services.

stories.title: India power demand rises as coal stocks remain low
stories.summary: India's power demand increased 11.7 percent from April to October, according to ICRA. Coal stocks at thermal plants averaged seven days as of 11 November, well below the normative requirement of 19 to 20 days. Generators currently have a limited buffer to manage sudden demand spikes.

stories.title: Heavy industries ministry rejects insurance bonds for battery projects
stories.summary: The ministry of heavy industries has rejected a proposal to allow insurance surety bonds instead of bank guarantees for a production-linked incentive scheme for battery manufacturing. The ministry shortlisted 22 bidders for the tender, which aims to build domestic cell manufacturing capacity after previous efforts faltered.

stories.title: Tata Steel plans hydrogen production project in Odisha - Construction Week India
Global coal consumption remains resilient due to China and India
stories.summary: Global coal consumption fell 10 percent between 2019 and 2025 across most countries, but rising demand from China and India has maintained resilience. Together, the two nations burn seven out of every 10 metric tons of coal used globally, masking a decline in consumption elsewhere.

stories.title: Nepal authorized to import 350 MW of power from India
stories.summary: The Central Electricity Authority of India has authorized the Nepal Electricity Authority to procure up to 350 MW of electricity from the Indian Energy Exchange. The approval allows for imports of up to 17 hours a day and is valid from 17 November 2026 to 31 July 2027.

stories.title: Supreme court stays Delhi municipal tax demand against NTPC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has stayed a 197 crore rupee tax demand issued by the Delhi Municipal Corporation to NTPC. The state-owned power producer must deposit 82 crore rupees with the court while the matter remains under review. The civic body is currently restrained from encashing the original demand draft.

stories.title: London car use forecast to rise by 10 percent
stories.summary: Car use in London is projected to increase by 10 percent over the next decade, according to an official forecast by the mayoralty. The modelling assumes no new transport policies are implemented. The city expects road congestion to slow buses and potentially force regular closures of underground stations.

stories.title: India maintains low profile at UN climate talks
stories.summary: India is participating in the UN climate talks in Turkey with a delegation of 152 people, smaller than those of Bangladesh, Pakistan or Nepal. The country has no dedicated promotional booth at the summit. It continues to champion climate funding rights for developing nations from the sidelines.

stories.title: COP31 highlights mountain climate risks
stories.summary: The proposal to include an agenda item on the impact of rising temperatures on high mountain ranges was rejected at COP31 in Antalya. Despite the procedural setback, the summit continues to spotlight the catastrophic effects of climate change on these regions and the urgent need for intervention.

stories.title: COP31 leaders discuss resilient cities
stories.summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum has launched initiatives for energy-efficient buildings, stating that climate action must deliver where people live. The presidency cited post-earthquake reconstruction in Turkey as a model for urban resilience. It remains to be seen if the proposed initiatives will receive the necessary financial backing.

stories.title: Bhubaneswar prepares for cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: The Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation has identified 93 cyclone shelters and placed emergency machinery on high alert ahead of cyclone Akvan. Officials have cancelled staff leave and prepared logistics for potential evacuations. Special teams have been formed to clear dangerous trees and electrical hazards from the city streets.

stories.title: India remains among most climate-vulnerable nations
stories.summary: A report citing the Climate Risk Index 2027 places India among the countries most affected by extreme weather over the last three decades. The findings have renewed questions regarding whether urban infrastructure and public systems are adequately designed to withstand repeated floods, heatwaves and cyclones.

stories.title: COP31 draft decision faces pushback
stories.summary: Countries are reviewing an 18-page draft cover decision from COP31, which has drawn criticism from nations seeking stronger action on the 1.5 degree Celsius threshold. The presidency stated the text is intended to support deliberations rather than reflect consensus. The document remains under active negotiation.

stories.title: Maharashtra halts Adani project over wildlife clearance
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Forest Department has ordered work to stop on Adani Green's 1,500 MW Tarali pumped storage project. The notice cites a lack of prior approval from the National Board for Wildlife. The company must explain why construction began without the required clearance within three days.

stories.title: Dreamteam raises 53 million dollars for AI-native CRM
stories.summary: Dreamteam has raised 53 million dollars to compete with Salesforce and HubSpot. The platform features a Company Brain that automatically logs emails and meetings to build a shared record of customer interactions. Four built-in AI agents are tasked with researching prospects and flagging potential deal risks.

stories.title: Enterprise AI faces ROI scrutiny
stories.summary: A recent summit in Canada revealed that the primary constraint for enterprise AI is organizational readiness rather than model access. Firms are increasingly demanding measurable outcomes for AI investments. Data readiness remains an operational discipline, as AI cannot reconstruct information that was never captured by the business.

stories.title: Synaps 2.0: Rethinking Architectural Design with AI
stories.summary: Architecture has always existed between imagination and representation. Long before a building takes physical form, it begins as an idea about space, structure, movement, and human experience. Architects translate these intentions into drawings, models, and technical documents, gradually transforming abstract concepts into something that can be understood, evaluated, and eventually

stories.title: Pegasus and Taisei launch 150 million dollar construction fund
stories.summary: Pegasus Tech Ventures and Taisei Corporation are establishing a 150 million dollar fund to invest in construction technology startups. The fund will operate for 10 years, targeting AI, robotics and digital twins. The partnership aims to improve construction productivity and create new business opportunities globally.

stories.title: Supersede raises $13M to enter construction market - Plastics News
Rayon V4 adds 3D modelling and AI agents
stories.summary: Rayon has released version 4 of its browser-based design software, adding 3D modelling and agentic AI to its 2D environment. The company aims to fill the market gap between AutoCAD and SketchUp. The new capabilities are currently available in beta, with a continued focus on interior design.

stories.title: Humyn Labs raises 47 million dollars for robotics data
stories.summary: India-based Humyn Labs has raised 47 million dollars in equity and debt to provide real-world data for training robots. The company aims to help U.S. firms build models capable of performing human tasks in physical environments. Demand for such training data is reportedly growing globally.

stories.title: SPZAORA integrates AI into interior design
stories.summary: SPZAORA is positioning itself to simplify the interior design process by combining architectural creativity with AI technology. The brand aims to address the growing demand for faster visualisation and efficient design planning among professionals. The company focuses on supporting architects through integrated design solutions.

stories.title: Autodesk and Neilsoft build joint go-to-market push around BIM and Digital Twins
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft are establishing a Centre of Excellence in Pune to expand their Building Information Modelling and Digital Twin offerings. The partnership combines Autodesk’s technology portfolio with Neilsoft’s engineering expertise to drive digital transformation across global markets. The companies are now formalising their collaborative sales strategy.

stories.title: Jikstecnolog chairman receives Presidential Commendation
stories.summary: Jikstecnolog chairman Choi Jong-bok received a Presidential Commendation in the Technology Innovation category at the 2026 SME Technology Management Innovation Competition. The Ministry of SMEs and Startups presents the award to recognize contributions to digital transformation and AI-based design innovation within the domestic industry.

stories.title: Neowise targets construction and defense with 3D reconstruction
stories.summary: NeoWise is applying AI to 2D video to render 3D environments for construction and defense applications. The company claims the technology can identify objects in low light and locate hidden infrastructure. It is currently developing a suite of image-processing, digital twin, and simulation solutions.

stories.title: Building healthier schools from the inside out
stories.summary: Sustainability in real estate is often treated as an optional design element that is value engineered out when budgets tighten. In Seattle, energy codes already mandate operational efficiency for new buildings. The focus is now shifting toward the impact of building materials on long-term health.

stories.title: Science Tokyo students win Good Design New Hope Award 2026
stories.summary: Two projects from Science Tokyo students received the Good Design New Hope Award 2026. The Haniyasu Kiln won in the Space Design category, while a 3D-printed assistive device for cell biology experiments was recognized in the System Design category. The Japan Institute of Design Promotion manages the awards.

stories.title: Neeraj Bhatia Is the New Director of Columbia GSAPP’s Urban Design Program - Columbia University
Revamped ArcStart program helps high school students explore architecture and build portfolios - U-M Detroit
Architecture school admission deadlines for 2027
stories.summary: Architecture schools in the U.S. and abroad have set their undergraduate and graduate admission deadlines for the fall 2027 term. Most applications are due in January and February. Schools are increasingly emphasizing holistic review processes that consider applicant backgrounds alongside traditional academic achievements.

stories.title: Cyprus begins procedures for Venice Biennale 2027
stories.summary: The Deputy Ministry of Culture and the Cyprus Architects’ Association have launched the selection process for the country’s participation in the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia 2027. The event remains a primary international institution for the architecture sector.

stories.title: Tyler School of Art and Architecture expands global residency
stories.summary: The Tyler School of Art and Architecture is launching a new global residency program for MFA students. Participants will spend three weeks at Temple University campuses in Rome or Kyoto. The program features mentorship from contemporary artists Jennifer Packer and Theaster Gates to integrate studio practice with cultural context.

stories.title: Mechanical contractors report mixed results with BIM-to-shop links
stories.summary: While 86 percent of mechanical contractors use BIM to model and link to fabrication software, only about half report that the integration works well. Fabrication lead times often span several weeks, making it difficult to keep shop schedules aligned with changing field installation sequences.

stories.title: Harvard GSD students propose alternatives to triumphal arch
stories.summary: Landscape architecture students at Harvard’s Graduate School of Design have designed two proposals for Memorial Circle in Washington, DC. The designs feature expansive water pools intended to cover the existing roundabout. The project aims to engage the public regarding the site of a proposed triumphal arch.

stories.title: EU countries urge exclusion of Russia from Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Ten European Union countries, led by Poland, have requested that the European Commission prevent Russia from participating in the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. The coalition argues that participation would normalize the war in Ukraine. The appeal follows a diplomatic note sent ahead of a ministerial meeting.

Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
research.summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world. New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological.

research.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
research.summary: A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature. Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing.
